corrections.text: The article quotes GitGuardian as saying testing stolen AI provider keys helps "make them harder to distinguish from normal server traffic." GitGuardian's React2STEAL report actually reads "making them harder to distinguish from normal server traffic" (a different verb form). The meaning is unchanged, but the quotation should reproduce GitGuardian's exact wording.

The article attributes the claim that GhostAction "resurfaced... modifying 92 workflows left behind from previous waves," with only "16% (124)" of affected repositories "effectively cleaned up" by early October, to GitGuardian's November 13 wfx-loot report ("That report also noted..."). That text does not appear in the wfx-loot report; it appears only in GitGuardian's November 20 React2STEAL report, which itself attributes the figures to a separate GitGuardian article, "GhostAction itself came back" (https://blog.gitguardian.com/ghostaction-github-actions-supply-chain-attack-returns/), not cited in this article's sources.
